# Introduction

This document is a clean, annotated workflow for quality control (QC) and analyses.  
Use comments in each section to explain what you did, why you did it, and any steps you ran but did not keep in the final clean code.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ANNOTATE: List package setup choices and why each package is needed.

# Install packages if needed (optional)
# install.packages(c("here", "dplyr", "tableone", "ggplot2"))

library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tableone)
library(ggplot2)

# Instead of setwd(), confirm project root with here::here().
here::here()
```

# 1) Upload dataset

```{r load-data}
# ANNOTATE: State data source and version/date used.

data_frame <- read.csv(here::here("DATA", "your_dataset.csv"))
```

# 2) Create adjusted follow-up year (if needed)

```{r adjusted-follow-up}
# ANNOTATE: Explain your baseline year definition for this variable/domain.
# Example reminder: baseline should be first collection year for the variable.

data_frame <- data_frame %>%
  mutate(adjusted_followup_year = followup_year - baseline_year + 1)
```

# 3) Check adjusted follow-up year

```{r check-adjusted-follow-up}
# ANNOTATE: Document QC checks and expected ranges.

summary(data_frame$adjusted_followup_year)
table(data_frame$adjusted_followup_year, useNA = "ifany")
```

# 4) Rename columns as needed

```{r rename-columns}
# ANNOTATE: List each rename and why it improves clarity or consistency.

data_frame <- data_frame %>%
  rename(
    participant_id = old_id_name
  )
```

# 5) Flowchart filtering (remove missing by analysis variable)

```{r flowchart-filtering}
# ANNOTATE: Explain inclusion/exclusion logic.

analysis_var <- subset(data_frame, !is.na(var_1))
```

# 6) Verify filtering and missingness

```{r check-missingness}
# ANNOTATE: Confirm filtered sample size and missingness checks.

nrow(analysis_var)
sapply(analysis_var[, c("var_1", "var_2", "var_3")], function(x) sum(is.na(x)))
```

# 7) Create Table 1 (tableone)

```{r tableone}
# ANNOTATE: Explain variable selections for descriptive table.

vars <- c("var_1", "var_2", "var_3")
table1 <- CreateTableOne(vars = vars, data = analysis_var)
print(table1, quote = FALSE, noSpaces = TRUE)
```

# 8) Check Table 1 for NAs

```{r check-tableone}
# ANNOTATE: Note any NA-related issues and how they were resolved.

colSums(is.na(analysis_var[, vars]))
```

# 9) QC graphs (histogram, box plot, etc.)

```{r qc-histogram}
# ANNOTATE: State what this plot checks and expected shape/outliers.

ggplot(analysis_var, aes(x = var_1)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30)
```

```{r qc-boxplot}
# ANNOTATE: Describe outlier handling decisions.

ggplot(analysis_var, aes(y = var_1)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```

# 10) Run analyses

```{r analyses}
# ANNOTATE: Explain model choice, covariates, and interpretation plan.

model_1 <- lm(outcome ~ var_1 + var_2 + adjusted_followup_year, data = analysis_var)
summary(model_1)
```

# 11) Interpretation notes

- ANNOTATE: For each key result, state what higher/lower values mean in domain terms.
- ANNOTATE: Explain sign and magnitude (for example, positive beta interpretation).
- ANNOTATE: Separate statistical interpretation from substantive interpretation.

# 12) Presentation checklist for review

- Include Table 1
- Include QC graphs (histogram, box plot, others as needed)
- Include annotated code comments explaining:
  - steps you took
  - why you took them
  - extra code you ran but excluded from clean code

# 13) Clean code vs messy code reminder

- Keep a **messy working script** for exploration/troubleshooting.
- Submit a **clean script/report** with required steps only (no extra exploratory code).
